Rhizopus shows much more extensive fuzzy growth all over the fruit - not matching the test image's localized stem-end infection. Let me check Phytophthora_Blight.
Phytophthora Blight shows dark discoloration on fruit but without the gray fuzzy sporulation seen in the test image. Let me check my 4th class - Anthracnose.

Anthracnose shows circular sunken lesions with concentric rings - completely different from the test image's diffuse stem-end decay with gray sporulation.

- **Test image**: Fruit with gray/white fuzzy sporulation at the calyx/stem end, brown decay spreading downward - classic Ghost Spot or calyx-end rot from Botrytis
- **Gray_Mold**: Matches perfectly - gray fuzzy growth at stem/calyx, brown decay spreading from infection site
- **Rhizopus_Soft_Rots**: Doesn't match - shows extensive fuzzy growth across entire fruit surface
- **Phytophthora_Blight**: Doesn't match - dark greasy discoloration without gray sporulation
- **Anthracnose**: Doesn't match - circular sunken lesions with concentric rings

The localized gray/white fuzzy sporulation at the calyx end with brown decay spreading downward is the hallmark of **Gray Mold** (Botrytis cinerea) on tomato fruit.
